findings.item: Family 003 'The quasi-Riemann hypothesis' (3 manuscripts). The same holds for every Dirichlet $L$-function, including $\zeta(s)$. A pole at $s=1$ for a principal character is allowed." Companion paper2.tex Theorem (line 73): "Every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $K$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>11/12$ ..." ($K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$). Siegel paper build/paper.tex Theorem (line 66): "There is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that every real zero $\beta\in(0,1)$ of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet $L$-function of conductor $q\ge3$ satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q\ge c$." findings.why_relevant: Criterion (ii) only, and remotely: these are zero-free regions for DEGREE-ONE L-functions (Dirichlet characters, Hecke Groessencharacters of Q(sqrt(-3))). L(E,s) for the seed is a degree-2 non-CM L-function (E has no CM; K=Q(sqrt(-7)), not Q(sqrt(-3))), so nothing here bounds or evaluates L''(E,1) or L(E^{-7},1), and nothing touches FIN/ORDER9/Q36 or Sha at any prime. The only conceivable indirect use is as an effective prime-counting input (primes l ≡ 1 mod p in dyadic ranges) when searching for Kurihara/production-symbol auxiliary primes l for the good-prime route or B.18; but the lab needs specific primes, not asymptotics, and classical Dirichlet zero-free regions already suffice for that. Kill tests: K-A n/a; K-GRADE: Lean-checked zero-free statements are LEAN_CHECKED, everything else IMPORTED_PREPRINT. Lab would still have to: nothing (no use identified).

findings.item: Family 029 'Primitive roots for every admissible integer base' (2 manuscripts). CLAIMED: build/sections/01-introduction.tex Theorem 1.1 (\label{thm:main}, l.17): "For every admissible integer $a$, there are constants $c_a>0$ and $x_a\ge2$ such that, for every real $x\ge x_a$, $\#\{p\text{ prime}:x<p<2x,\ p\nmid a,\ \ord_p(a)=p-1\}\ge c_a\frac{x}{(\log x)^2}$." Theorem 1.2 (\label{thm:hecke-zero-free}, l.38): "Let $F$ be a cyclotomic number field containing $\mu_{12}$. For every finite-order Hecke character $\eta$ of $F$, the meromorphic continuation of $L_F(s,\eta)$ has no zeros in $\re s>1-10^{-6}$." (text: 'The principal character is included, with its pole at $s=1$ permitted. The width is common to all fields and characters in the statement, with no conductor or height cutoff.') No Lean formalization listed. Companion 'Simultaneous primitive roots' is explicitly conditional on four inputs from this paper.
findings.location: preprints/Primitive-roots-for-every-admissible-integer-base-October-4-2026/build/sections/01-introduction.tex (Thm 1.1 l.17, Thm 1.2 l.38); build/sections/06-zero-free.tex (Prop. zero-density l.165)
findings.why_relevant: Criterion (ii)/(iii), remote. Theorem 1.2 is a uniform zero-free strip for finite-order Hecke L-functions of cyclotomic fields containing mu_12 (hence effective Chebotarev for ABELIAN extensions of such fields). The Frobenius conditions needed for Kolyvagin/Kurihara auxiliary primes (Frob_l in a prescribed class of Gal(Q(E[p])/Q), with rho-bar_p(G_Q) ⊇ SL2(F_p) recorded for p=2243,5843) are non-abelian, so Thm 1.2 does not reach them; the abelian part (l ≡ 1 mod p^k) is already covered by classical theory. No bearing on FIN/ORDER9/Q36/TH. It is the sole analytic input of family 142 (see that entry), so any use of 142 inherits this unrefereed claim.

findings.item: Family 142 'Deterministic polynomial factorization over prime fields' (1 manuscript). CLAIMED: build/sections/00-introduction.tex Theorem 1.1 (\label{thm:factorization}, l.27): "There is a uniform deterministic algorithm that, given a prime $p$ in binary and a nonzero dense polynomial $f\in\Fp[x]$ of degree $n$, outputs its leading coefficient and its distinct monic irreducible factors with their multiplicities in $O\bigl(((n+1)\lceil\log_2p\rceil)^{10^{12}}\bigr)$ bit operations, with absolute implied constant. ... The algorithm uses no randomness, integer-factorization oracle, primitive-root oracle, or GRH assumption." (c) OAI-internal import: build/sections/10-analytic.tex l.9: "\begin{theorem}[\cite{OpenAIPrimitive26}, Theorem~1.2] For every cyclotomic number field $K$ containing the twelfth roots of unity, and every finite-order Hecke character $\chi$ of $K$, the Hecke $L$-function $L_K(s,\chi)$ has no zero in $\Re s>1-\delta,\ \delta=10^{-6}$." i.e. depends on family 029 (not withdrawn/revised per history.md). No Lean.
findings.location: preprints/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields-October-4-2026/build/sections/00-introduction.tex (Thm 1.1 l.27, Thm 1.2 'reduction' l.61); build/sections/10-analytic.tex (imported Thm l.9)
findings.why_relevant: Criterion (iii) (linear algebra over F_p / Hecke-eigenvector isolation via characteristic-polynomial factorization), but only in principle: the exponent 10^12 makes it useless in practice, and randomized Cantor–Zassenhaus/Berlekamp (polynomial expected time, unconditional) already handle every F_p factorization the lab's Brandt-module, modular-symbol or Kurihara-witness computations need. Offers no reduction of the seed-scale Brandt enumeration (~5e14 classes) or of the 31.6k–74k core-hour B.18 computation. Not relevant to FIN/ORDER9/Q36/TH. Lab would have to do nothing with it.

findings.item: Families 107/109/130 (asymptotic arithmetic complexity). 107 CLAIMED: preprints/Matrix-Multiplication-Nine-Fourths-October-2-2026/build/paper.tex Theorem 1.1 (l.45): "For every $\eps>0$, two $n\times n$ complex matrices can be multiplied using $O_\eps(n^{9/4+\eps})$ arithmetic operations. In particular, $\omega\leq9/4$." (secondary writeups: omega<2.258 char 0; omega<2.371054886006746 every field). 109 CLAIMED (abstract): integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, $\kappa=2^{-182}$. 130 CLAIMED (abstract): DFT in $O(n(\log n)^{1-10^{-13}})$ operations. Lean docs listed for 107 and 130 (lean/docs/107.md, 130.md).
findings.why_relevant: Criterion (iii) nominally (linear algebra / FFT underlying Brandt-matrix and modular-symbol computations), but all three are asymptotic/galactic bounds (9/4 is far worse than Strassen-level practical algorithms already in BLAS/FLINT; the saving factors 2^{-182} and 10^{-13} are unobservable). They cannot reduce any named lab cost (Brandt class-set enumeration, Hecke-eigenvector isolation, B.18 core-hours). No bearing on FIN/ORDER9/Q36/TH.

findings.item: Family 032 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' + Family 001 'Milne's rationality conjecture'. 032 CLAIMED: build/sections/01-introduction.tex Theorem (\label{thm:cm}, l.17): "Let $A$ be a complex CM abelian variety. For every integer $p\geq0$, the Betti cycle-class map $\operatorname{cl}_B:\CH^p(A)_{\Q}\longrightarrow H^{2p}(A,\Q)\cap H^{p,p}(A)$ is surjective ..." (consequences claimed: generalized Hodge for CM AV, Tate for AV over finite fields, Hodge standard conjecture). 001 CLAIMED: build/sections/00_intro.tex Theorem (\label{thm:main}, l.29): "Let $A/\Qbar$ be an abelian variety of dimension $d$ with good reduction $A_0/\F$ at $w$. ... $\gamma\in H^{2r}(A(\C),\Q(r))$ ... a rational Hodge class. For every list of Cartier divisors $D_1,\ldots,D_{d-r}$ on $A_0$, there is a number $q\in\Q$ such that $\Tr_\ell(\gamma_{0,\ell}\cdots)$ [equals q in every prime-to-p and crystalline realization]." Companions 'Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers' (Thms 'Split Weil sixfolds' l.79, 'Quadratic actions in dimension at most five' l.88: Hodge for A^m, A of dim<=5 with imaginary-quadratic action) and 'Abelian covers, Gale correspondences...' (Thm 'Powers of abelian-cover Jacobians' l.104: (Jac(C_s) x M)^N at tensor-Hodge-generic s, M CM). Dependencies (c): 032 cites OAI Milne paper (references.bib OpenAIMilneRationality2026) and 001 abstract says it uses 'the Hodge theorem for CM abelian varieties' (mutual OAI dependency); 'Weil classes' says it 'uses the companion theorem on the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties'. history.md (Oct 7): three manuscripts of this family WITHDRAWN for a sign error ('Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds' and two dependents); the surviving 032/001 papers were re-dated Oct 6/7 'updating citations' and contain no reference to the eightfold paper (grep 'eightfold' in 032 sections: none). No Lean for 032 or 001.

findings.why_relevant: Criterion (i) 'Hodge/Tate conjectures for CM abelian varieties or products of elliptic curves'. Hypothesis check: the seed E has NO CM and E^{-7} is not CM either, so Thm thm:cm does not apply to E, E^{-7}, E x E^{-7} or Res_{K/Q} E; the 'quadratic actions in dim<=5' theorem needs an imaginary-quadratic action, which E x E^{-7} lacks (End^0 = Q x Q). Even where Hodge/Tate holds, it says nothing about Sha, L''(E,1), periods or heights, so no path to FIN/ORDER9/Q36 or lemma TH. Grade IMPORTED_PREPRINT with an extra flag: the family suffered three withdrawals on Oct 7 for a sign error; the survivors' independence from the flawed construction is asserted only by the version notes.

findings.item: Family 015 'Torus-packet equidistribution in prime, quartic, and sextic degrees' (3 manuscripts). Different group, different field type, and equidistribution cannot replace the unaffordable exact enumeration (~5e14 classes) or certify M_2(p) != 0 at a specific p. No path to FIN/ORDER9/Q36/TH.
